review.notes: The selected verb has the inherited se- apart, par prepare/procure, and verbal -ate structure. Prepare supplies the companion parare family, and the University of Michigan teaching exercise independently includes separate in the -ate family. The exact first join is the bound stem separ, not an invented standalone verb; the second yields separate. Par.prepare is kept distinct from compare par.equal. The whole separating action remains the definition; the historical preparation gloss is not a claim that separation means preparation or equalization. This review concerns the verb rather than automatically reusing its analysis for a noun or adjective sense.
